saints.name: St. Monica
saints.title: Widow
saints.shortBlurb: The mother of St. Augustine, whose tears and prayers over many years won her son to Christ…
biography: Born about 331 at Thagaste in Numidia, of Berber stock, Monica was married to Patricius, a pagan town official of violent temper and loose life, whom she bore with patience and finally won to baptism before his death. Among their children was Augustine, who as a student at Carthage fell into Manichaeism and broke her heart.

For some seventeen years she prayed and wept for his conversion. When a bishop, wearied by her entreaties, answered her, 'the child of those tears shall never perish,' she received the words as an oracle. She followed Augustine from Africa to Rome and on to Milan, where through the ministry of St. Ambrose he was converted and baptized at Easter 387.

At Ostia, awaiting the voyage home, mother and son were lifted together at a window into a foretaste of heaven, as the Confessions records. There she died in that same year 387, asking only to be remembered at the altar. Her relics were brought to Rome in 1430 and rest in the church of Sant'Agostino; the long-suffering wife and importunate mother is honoured as patron of wives and mothers.
saints.knownFor: Her persevering prayer for her son's conversion.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 May
